title: Gregor Mendel's pea plant experiments
summary: Gregor Mendel began breeding experiments with garden peas in 1856, according to a timeline in a 2022 article in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. His article 'Versuche über Pflanzen-Hybriden' appeared in 1866 in the Proceedings of the Natural History Society in Brno, and its results were ignored at the time. The Mendel Museum of Masaryk University says he formulated the laws of heredity from his pea experiments in the Augustinian abbey in old Brno.

uncertainty.note: Mendel began his systematic pea breeding experiments at St. Thomas's Abbey in 1856, presented his findings in 1865, and published them in the 1866 volume of the Natural History Society of Brünn proceedings.

as_recorded.value: manuscript of his 1866 article entitled “Versuche über Pflanzen-Hybriden” (“Experiments on plant hybrids”)
Gregor Johann Mendel conducted his experiments with peas and formulated the groundbreaking laws of heredity and genetics

where.modern_name: Brno, South Moravian Region, Czech Republic
where.historical_name: Brünn, Margraviate of Moravia, Austrian Empire

importance.justification: Mendel's experiments with peas led to the laws of heredity, which the Mendel Museum of Masaryk University calls groundbreaking for genetics.

related.because: Mendel's laws of inheritance provided the particulate mechanism of heredity that Darwin's theory of natural selection initially lacked.
Mendel's concept of inherited particulate factors directly anticipated the discovery of the molecular gene and the DNA double helix.

beats.caption: In the monastery garden in Brno, Gregor Mendel begins eight years of controlled hybridization experiments with garden peas.
Mendel publishes his findings formulating the laws of segregation and independent assortment, founding modern genetics.
